name: Should I change my kitchen layout or keep the existing footprint?

mainEntity.name: Should I change my kitchen layout or keep the existing footprint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keeping your existing layout is significantly faster and less expensive, but altering it is worth the investment if your current setup restricts daily use. If your kitchen lacks adequate counter space, blocks workflow between the stove and refrigerator, or feels isolated from adjacent living areas, moving walls or relocating appliances creates a more functional environment. However, changing the layout requires altering electrical circuits, supply lines, and drain piping, which extends project timelines and requires additional drywall finishing. If storage and aesthetic updates are your main goals, retaining your current walls and plumbing points delivers substantial visual improvements while controlling labor demands.
acceptedAnswer.description: Keep your layout if your workflow functions well and you want to save time and budget. Change it if you need better storage, expanded counter space, or an open concept.
